convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom for both EF_distance and Flat-Trend indicators (custom indicators not available as built-in MT5 functions). Depends on external SmoothAlgorithms.mqh and TradeAlgorithms.mqh libraries for smoothing algorithms and trade execution logic. Multi-indicator signal confirmation adds complexity.

derived_values.name: Volatility threshold from Flat-Trend buffer
derived_values.formula: Vol[0] compared against Volatil enum (V1=0, V2=1, V3=2)
derived_values.used_by: Entry signal gate - buy/sell only when Vol[0]>=Volatil

other_exits: Opposite signal closes existing position: sell signal triggers BUY_Close, buy signal triggers SELL_Close, gated by BuyPosClose/SellPosClose input flags

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MM parameter: negative values = fixed lot size (e.g. -0.1 = 0.1 lots), positive values = share of deposit fraction. The TradeAlgorithms.mqh library handles this conditional logic internally.

custom_logic_notes: The EF_distance indicator produces a smoothed price line. Entry logic detects a 'turn' in the EF_distance line: Value[1]<Value[2] means the line was declining (bar-1 below bar-2), and Value[0]>Value[1] means it has turned up at current bar - this triggers buy. Conversely, Value[1]>Value[2] with Value[0]<Value[1] triggers sell. The Flat-Trend indicator acts as a volatility filter: trades only execute when its buffer value >= the Volatil enum threshold. SignalBar=1 means signals are read from bar index 1 (last completed bar), not bar 0 (forming bar). The Recount flag ensures data is re-fetched if CopyBuffer fails. The BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/BuyPosClose/SellPosClose input booleans act as master switches for each trade direction and exit type.
python_conversion_notes: Two custom indicators (EF_distance, Flat-Trend) must be ported or replaced. SmoothAlgorithms.mqh provides XMA class with GetStartBars() and various smoothing methods (LWMA etc) - these map to standard moving average implementations. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen/SellPositionOpen/BuyPositionClose/SellPositionClose and helper functions (LoadHistory, GlobalVariableDel_, CIsNewBar) - these must be reimplemented in Python. The conditional MM sizing (negative=fixed lots, positive=deposit fraction) needs careful handling. The EF_distance turning-point logic is straightforward to replicate. The Flat-Trend volatility filter requires porting both StDev and ATR smoothed calculations. Entry signals use bars [0],[1],[2] relative to SignalBar, so the logic operates on the 3 most recent completed bars by default.
